supA.name: Anterior division of the superior trunk

supP.name: Posterior division of the superior trunk

midA.name: Anterior division of the middle trunk

midP.name: Posterior division of the middle trunk

infA.name: Anterior division of the inferior trunk

infP.name: Posterior division of the inferior trunk

mca.name: Medial cutaneous nerve of the arm

mcf.name: Medial cutaneous nerve of the forearm

C5.d: Ventral ramus of C5. Joins C6 to form the superior trunk.
C5.c: Gives off the dorsal scapular nerve and part of the long thoracic nerve.

C6.d: Ventral ramus of C6. Joins C5 to form the superior trunk.
C6.c: Gives part of the long thoracic nerve.

C7.d: Ventral ramus of C7. Carries on alone as the middle trunk.
C7.c: Gives part of the long thoracic nerve.

C8.d: Ventral ramus of C8. Joins T1 to form the inferior trunk.

T1.d: Ventral ramus of T1. Joins C8 to form the inferior trunk.

sup.c: The only trunk that gives off a nerve: the suprascapular nerve.

supA.d: Joins the anterior division of the middle trunk to form the lateral cord.
supA.c: No nerves branch off the divisions. Anterior divisions → the flexor (front) compartments.

midA.d: Joins the anterior division of the superior trunk to form the lateral cord.
midA.c: No nerves branch off the divisions. Anterior divisions → the flexor (front) compartments.

infA.d: Carries on alone as the medial cord.
infA.c: No nerves branch off the divisions. Anterior divisions → the flexor (front) compartments.

supP.d: One of the three posterior divisions that form the posterior cord.
supP.c: No nerves branch off the divisions. Posterior divisions → the extensor (back) compartments.

midP.d: One of the three posterior divisions that form the posterior cord.
midP.c: No nerves branch off the divisions. Posterior divisions → the extensor (back) compartments.

infP.d: One of the three posterior divisions that form the posterior cord (the \ of the drawing).
infP.c: No nerves branch off the divisions. Posterior divisions → the extensor (back) compartments.

lat.d: Anterior divisions of the superior + middle trunks. Named for where it sits around the axillary artery.
lat.c: Ends as the musculocutaneous nerve and the lateral root of the median nerve. Gives off the lateral pectoral nerve.

post.d: All three posterior divisions. Named for where it sits around the axillary artery.
post.c: Ends as the axillary and radial nerves. Gives off the upper subscapular, thoracodorsal and lower subscapular nerves.

med.d: Anterior division of the inferior trunk, carrying on alone. Named for where it sits around the axillary artery.
med.c: Ends as the ulnar nerve and the medial root of the median nerve. Gives off the medial pectoral and the medial cutaneous nerves of the arm and forearm.

mc.m: All of the anterior arm: pierces coracobrachialis, then runs between biceps and brachialis
mc.s: Lateral forearm (ends as the lateral cutaneous nerve of the forearm)

medn.m: Most forearm flexors, the thenar muscles and lumbricals 1-2. Nothing in the arm
medn.c: A lateral root from the lateral cord and a medial root from the medial cord join to form it: the middle of the "M".

uln.m: Flexor carpi ulnaris, the medial half of flexor digitorum profundus and most intrinsic hand muscles. Nothing in the arm

ax.c: A surgical neck fracture of the humerus threatens it.

rad.m: Extensors of the back of the arm and forearm
rad.c: A humeral shaft fracture threatens it. Like the median nerve, it carries every root (C5-T1).

ds.c: Pierces the middle scalene, then runs back to the rhomboids.

lt.m: Serratus anterior (runs along its superficial surface)

lp.c: Runs above and medial to pectoralis minor.

mp.c: Pierces pectoralis minor on its way to pectoralis major.

mca.s: Skin of the medial arm and axilla, upper forearm

mcf.s: Skin of the medial and anterior forearm

td.c: Also called the middle subscapular nerve.

uln: Flexes wrist; flexes IP joints in digits 4-5
Flex the MCP joint; extend the IP joints
medn: Flexes wrist; flexes IP joints in digits 2-3
Flexes wrist; flexes MCP & IP joint of digit 1
Flex the MCP joint; extend the IP joints
rad: Weakly flexes the forearm; strongest in mid-pronated position ("drinking muscle")
Extends and abducts wrist; active during fist clenching
Extends and adducts wrist; active during fist clenching
Extends digit 5 (MCP joint primarily, IP joints secondarily); also extends wrist
Extends MCP joints primarily, IP joints secondarily (digits 2-5); also extends wrist
Together extend elbow; long head extends shoulder joint and resists shoulder dislocation
mc: Strong supinator; flexes forearm; weak shoulder flexor; resists dislocation
Flexes arm; adducts arm; resists dislocation
ax: Anterior head: flexes and medially rotates arm; middle head: abducts arm; posterior head: extends and laterally rotates arm
Lateral rotation of arm; stabilizes glenohumeral joint
ss: Lateral rotation of arm; stabilizes glenohumeral joint
First 15 degrees of arm abduction; stabilizes glenohumeral joint
td: Extends, adducts and medially rotates humerus
ds: Elevates scapula; rotates to depress glenoid cavity
Retract scapula; rotate to depress glenoid cavity; fix scapula to thoracic wall
Retract scapula; rotate to depress glenoid cavity; fix scapula to thoracic wall
lp: Adducts, flexes and medially rotates humerus
per our table; Netter lists the medial pectoral nerve only
Stabilizes scapula by drawing it inferiorly and anteriorly against thoracic wall
mp: Adducts, flexes and medially rotates humerus
Stabilizes scapula by drawing it inferiorly and anteriorly against thoracic wall
us: Medially rotates arm; stabilizes glenohumeral joint
ls: Medially rotates arm; stabilizes glenohumeral joint

MOVES.rad: Extends the arm and the forearm (triceps), the wrist, the fingers and the thumb; supinates the forearm (supinator); brachioradialis flexes the elbow in mid-pronation. Cut it: wrist drop
MOVES.mc: Flexes the elbow (brachialis, biceps) and supinates the forearm (biceps); flexes the arm at the shoulder (coracobrachialis)
MOVES.ax: Abducts the arm past the first 15° (deltoid); flexes, extends and rotates it (deltoid), laterally rotates it (teres minor)
MOVES.medn: Pronates the forearm; flexes the wrist and the fingers (FDS, lateral FDP, FPL); abducts and opposes the thumb; lumbricals 1 and 2 flex the index and middle MCPs. Cut it: hand of benediction, ape hand
MOVES.uln: Flexes and adducts the wrist (FCU); flexes the ring and little fingers (medial FDP); abducts and adducts the fingers (interossei); adducts the thumb; moves the little finger (hypothenar). Cut it: claw hand
MOVES.ss: Starts abduction of the arm, the first 15° (supraspinatus); laterally rotates the arm (infraspinatus)
MOVES.td: Adducts, extends and medially rotates the arm
MOVES.lt: Protracts the scapula and holds it to the chest wall. Cut it: winged scapula
MOVES.lp: Adducts, flexes and medially rotates the arm (pectoralis major); draws the scapula forward and down (pectoralis minor)
MOVES.mp: Adducts, flexes and medially rotates the arm (pectoralis major); draws the scapula forward and down (pectoralis minor)
MOVES.ls: Medially rotates and adducts the arm
